text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co. improperly handled debt collection procedures with about 22,000 people across the country since last summer, a source familiar with a court-ordered filing said Friday.

Sears misled many of its once-bankrupt credit card holders into believing they had to repay their debts to the company even though the debts had been wiped out by a bankruptcy court, a judge ruled last month.

In the first of three court-ordered reports that was due Friday, Sears said it failed to file required debt repayment agreements reached with 22,464 people over the last 10 months, the source told Reuters.
The list of debtors is the first indication of the national breadth of Sears' debt collection activities, which the company has admitted were "flawed."
Sears, the nation's second-largest retailer, has agreed to pay refunds to debtors who were wronged by its collection activities and give each a $100 gift certificate.
The company, based in Hoffman Estates, Ill., has not tallied up how much the refunds will cost, but analysts estimated it could be tens of millions of dollars or more.
A U.S. Bankruptcy Court judge in Boston indicated last month she may order Sears to pay punitive damages of $1.4 million to just one debtor, according to a report in the Boston Globe.
On April 16, the judge ordered Sears to stop the practice in Massachusetts, where more than 2,700 customers entered such agreements over a two-year period ended in January.
About 27 states are investigating Sears and considering coordinating efforts, said Chris Barry-Smith, an assistant attorney general in Massachusetts. Penalties by states are also possible.
The Justice Department is also investigating.
"I think this list will identify different areas in the country where this has happened most," said Susan Poswistilo, an assistant U.S. attorney in Massachusetts.
State officials also will use the list to identify how many debtors would qualify for restitution from Sears, she said.

Sears is continuing its review of its collection procedures and will provide officials by June 3 with a list of debtors who entered into restitution agreements from July 1994 through July 1996. The number of affected debtors may change.
In the third report, Sears will identify all such debtors nationwide from January 1992 through June 1994.
